svg.title: Proof. In any nonnegative factorization T = AB with r factors let Si = {l: Ail> 0}. If Si ⊆Sj, the zero Tjj implies Blj = 0 for every l∈Sj, hence Tij = 0. This contradicts Tij > 0 for i ̸= j. Thus the m supports are an antichain. To recall the counting bound without relying on a citation, a uniformly random permutation of r elements has at most one initial segment belonging to an antichain. A set S is such an initial segment with probability (︁r |S| )︁−1. Taking expectations yields ∑︁ i (︁r |Si| )︁−1 ≤1, hence m ≤ (︁ r ⌊r/2⌋ )︁, the classical Sperner bound[14]. Apply this to every slice of (1).
